 Around eight companies have fixed Wednesday as the record date for their respective dividends, effectively making today the last day for interested investors to buy the shares of the companies to be eligible for the dividend payouts.
 Under Sebi’s T+1 settlement cycle, investors need to purchase a company’s shares at least one trading day before the record date to ensure the shares are credited to their demat accounts in time, and they become eligible for the corporate action. Accordingly, today is the last opportunity for investors to buy the shares so that they are credited to their accounts by the record date (November 4), making them eligible for the dividend.
 Asian Paints dividend
Earlier last month, Asian Paints declared an interim dividend of Rs 5.75 per share of Re 1 face value for FY27, with November 4 (Wednesday) set as the record date to determine eligible shareholders.
The said dividend will be paid by November 13 (Friday) to those shareholders who own the shares as on the record date. The stock has a dividend yield of 1.17%, according to data on Trendlyne.
 Also read | Asian Paints Q2 Results: Net profit rises 7% YoY to Rs 1,068 crore; firm announces Rs 5.75/share dividend 
 Live Events
 Coal India dividend
 Coal India accounts for the highest dividend payout among all the stocks turning ex-record date for dividends tomorrow. The company has fixed Wednesday as the record date for its second interim dividend of Rs 10.25 apiece for the financial year 2027.
The said dividend will be paid to the eligible shareholders on or before November 27. The company has declared 36 dividends since 2011, and the stock has a dividend yield of more than 6.5%.
 Also read | Diwali stock picks: SBI Securities lists 11 stocks with up to 22% upside potential. Do you own any? 
 Other dividend stocks
 Godrej Consumer Products will pay an interim dividend of Rs 5 per share to its shareholders. The company has declared 84 dividends since October 30 and the stock has a dividend yield of nearly 2.5%.
 Privi Speciality Chemicals will also pay an interim dividend of Rs 5 per share, while Symphony will pay an interim dividend of Rs 2 per share. Other stocks with Wednesday as the record date for dividends include Vaibhav Global (Rs 1.5 per share), Praruh Technologies (Rs 1 per share) and Silver Touch Technologies (Rs 0.1 per share).

 Smallcap pharma firm Concord Biotech , which was backed by late ace investor Rakesh Jhunjhunwala , has fixed November 4 (Wednesday) as the record date for its 1:1 bonus issue , making today the last day for investors to buy the stock and become eligible for the bonus shares.
 Only those shareholders who hold Concord Biotech shares in their demat accounts as of Wednesday will be eligible to receive the bonus shares. As per Sebi's T+1 settlement cycle, investors must buy the company's shares at least one trading day before the record date for them to be credited to their demat accounts and qualify for the bonus issue. This makes today the last day to buy the stock to be eligible for the bonus shares.
 Also read | Bonus issues, stock splits, dividends: Infosys, Asian Paints among over 40 stocks turning ex-date this week 
 All about Concord Biotech’s bonus issue
Concord Biotech announced in September that its board of directors considered and approved the issuance of bonus shares in the ratio of 1:1 by capitalising the company’s share premium account. The company would issue 10.46 crore bonus shares with a face value of Re 1 each as part of the corporate action.
Later in October, Concord Biotech fixed November 4 as the record date for the purpose of determining the eligibility of shareholders set to receive the bonus shares, which will be allotted by November 5 (Thursday).
 Live Events
A bonus issue consists of free shares distributed by a company from its reserves and is often seen as a sign of strong financial health and growth prospects. While the issue of bonus shares increases the total number of outstanding shares, it does not change the company’s market capitalisation. However, it can improve liquidity and affordability, allowing more investors to add shares of the company to their portfolio. A 1:1 bonus issue means that eligible shareholders will get one bonus share for every single share held in the company as on the record date.
 Also read | Diwali 2026: 77 stocks knock down D-St bears to deliver multibagger returns of up to 4,700% in a year 
 Rakesh Jhunjhunwala's investment in Concord Biotech
Ace investor Rakesh Jhunjhunwala, often called India's Warren Buffet, first invested in Concord Biotech in 2004 and later helped the company's founder in buying back the company from pharma major Mylan in 2009. His investment firm RARE Enterprises stayed invested in the company during its Rs 1,551 crore IPO in 2023.
The son of an income tax officer, Jhunjhunwala started making his mark on Dalal Street in 1985, when the BSE Sensex was young, at a mere 150 level. Starting his career with a humble Rs 5,000, Jhunjhunwala built a multi-billion dollar portfolio on Dalal Street. A qualified Chartered Accountant, he invested in both his own name and his wife, Rekha Jhunjhunwala. He favoured stocks in the finance, tech, retail and pharma sectors.
He passed away at the age of 62 on August 14, 2022, following a cardiac arrest. He was suffering from multiple health problems related to the heart, diabetes and kidney, according to sources.
Rakesh Jhunjhunwala and associates held around 24% stake in Concord Biotech as of the end of the September quarter of FY27, according to data on Trendlyne.
 Also read | Bitcoin rattled by biggest crypto heist in history! Why Warren Buffett and Charlie Munger hated cryptocurrency 
 Concord Biotech share price
Concord Biotech shares have fallen more than 11% in one week and over 15% in one month, with the stock overall being down nearly 13% in 2026 so far.
The shares of the company have dropped 19% in the past one year, but delivered positive returns of a little over 3% in three years. It has a market capitalisation of around Rs 12,172 crore.

docs.title: Chinese stocks fall as investors unimpressed by fresh market support measures
docs.text:
Chinese stocks fell on Tuesday as investors sold energy and technology shares , with regulators' latest measures to stabilise the country's struggling capital markets failing to revive sentiment.
 The blue-chip CSI300 Index and the benchmark Shanghai Composite Index both declined around 1% in early trade, erasing gains from the previous session. Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index was largely unchanged, Reuters reported.
 As on 03 Nov 2026, 02:30 AM IST

Chinese regulators announced a series of measures on Monday to support the stock market, including swap operations and an upgrade to a lending facility aimed at encouraging listed companies to buy back their shares, according to Reuters.
 Read more: Global Market Today: Asian stocks slide as US chip selloff deepens 
The measures came after the CSI300 slumped 8.5% in October, marking its worst monthly performance in more than a decade, as a sustained selloff in technology stocks weighed on investor sentiment.
 Live Events
However, the latest policy support fell short of market expectations, Reuters reported, citing Chen Jiande, a fund manager at Fujian Tianlang Asset Management. Investors holding battered technology stocks were using any market rebound as an opportunity to exit their positions, he added.
The technology-focused STAR Composite Index dropped 1.6%, reflecting continued weakness in the sector.
 Read more: US stocks today: Nasdaq ends over 1% lower as AI worries persist 
Investor sentiment was also affected by concerns over the financial health of state-owned developer Zhuhai Huafa Group. Reports that the company was seeking extensions on some bank loans added to concerns about financial risks in China's property sector, Reuters reported.
Meanwhile, Chinese government bond yields remained largely steady in early trade. Yields on 10-year and 30-year government bonds edged down around 0.3 basis points each, according to Reuters.

docs.title: Marico shares jump 6% as strong Q2 puts growth story in overdrive, sparks bullish calls
docs.text:
Shares of Marico jumped 6% to Rs 845 on the NSE on Tuesday after the FMCG major reported a 31% year-on-year (YoY) increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 550 crore for the second quarter of the ongoing FY27, with brokerages raising target prices for the stock.
 Marico said that its revenue from operations increased 12% YoY to Rs 3,897 crore during the July-September quarter of the financial year 2027, from Rs 3,450 crore reported in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year, according to a filing on the exchange released on Monday. Its earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) increased 27% YoY to Rs 709 crore, against Rs 560 crore in the year-ago quarter. EBITDA margin expanded 200 basis points to 18.2% from 16.2% in Q2 FY26.
Marico's gross margin expanded approximately 600 basis points year-on-year, supported by moderation in copra prices and a favourable portfolio mix. The company's India business recorded 10% underlying volume growth, while its international business reported 13% constant currency growth (CCG).
 Also Read | Marico Q2 Results: Net profit jumps 31% YoY to Rs 550 crore, revenue rises 12% 
 Jefferies on Marico share price
Jefferies maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on the shares of Marico but raised its target price to Rs 1,035 apiece from Rs 1,000 apiece. The latest target price implies 29% upside potential for what the international brokerage called ‘Mr Consistent is getting even better’.
 Live Events
Jefferies said the compounding flywheel continues, with volume and EBITDA growth at multi-year highs. The core portfolio grew strongly, further supported by robust performance in foods and PPC. The company’s management raised FY27 guidance and, interestingly, now expects to hit its Rs 200 billion FY30 revenue target a year early, Jefferies noted. “Clearly, at a time when peers are seeing patchy trends, Marico stands out as a compounding machine, as reflected in its premium valuation relative to peers,” the international brokerage said.
In its base case, Jefferies forecast a 10% CAGR in revenue with 14% CAGR in earnings over FY26-29.
 Systematix on Marico share price
Systematix Institutional Equities maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on the shares of Marico with a target price of Rs 960 apiece. The brokerage noted that the company delivered another quarter of healthy earnings beat with Q2 operating results ahead of estimates.
Marico remains in a sweet spot of robust volume growth (7-11% over the past six quarters) supplemented by double-digit topline growth, cherry-topped with a margin rebound. With Parachute pricing easing in FY27 as copra moderates, we expect sturdy volume growth to sustain going forward,” it said, naming the FMCG major a preferred pick, one of few large-cap names growing earnings at FY26-FY29 CAGR of 17% yet available at FY28E P/E of 40x.
 Dolat Capital on Marico share price
Dolat Capital upgraded its rating on the shares of Marico to ‘Buy’ and raised the target price to Rs 1,025 apiece. It noted that the company delivered healthy growth across its core portfolio along with improving contribution from newer businesses.
The sharp improvement in profitability, coupled with management’s upgraded growth outlook, provides greater confidence in the sustainability of its growth, it added.
 Also Read | Marico profit jumps 31%, flags rising input costs amid West Asia woes 
 Marico share price
Marico shares jumped 3% in a week and more than 2% in a month, with the stock overall being up more than 5% in 2026 so far. This comes even as the broader Nifty Midcap 50 index dropped 4% at the same time amid multiple headwinds.
The shares of the FMCG major have gained around 11% in one year. In the longer term, the stock delivered positive returns of more than 51% in three years and 44% in five years. The company has a market capitalisation of nearly Rs 1.04 lakh crore.

docs.title: NBFCs redesign lending models ahead of revolving credit curbs
docs.text:
Mumbai: Non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) are developing alternative loan products to replace revolving credit facilities ahead of the Reserve Bank of India 's proposed restrictions, seeking to protect lending volumes and retain customers while moving towards term-loan structures.
 Bajaj Finance has introduced new term-loan variants, while Tata Capital has begun piloting modified flexi-loan products and plans further trials this month.
The RBI's August draft proposes that NBFCs, except authorised credit card issuers, offer only term loans. These may be disbursed in instalments but must follow a predetermined repayment schedule; the repaid principal cannot replenish the sanctioned limit. Revolving facilities, by contrast, let borrowers draw, repay and borrow again within an approved limit, an arrangement particularly useful for working capital needs.
"We are already launching a set of different variants of term loans on November 1st which do not allow withdrawal," Rajeev Jain, vice chairman and managing director of Bajaj Finance, said during its October 19 earnings call.
Jain said a complete ban could temporarily affect assets under management and cause a marginal compression in net interest margins and profitability. However, the company is preparing alternatives rather than waiting for the RBI's final decision.
 Live Events
Tata Capital expects to convert more than half of its flexi-credit portfolio into modified products without a revolving facility. Managing director and CEO Rajiv Sabharwal said the company had already tested some alternatives and would begin testing the remaining variants in early November.
"Our modified products are almost at a similar price like the flexi loans," Sabharwal said during the October 27 earnings call. He added that existing flexi loans carry higher interest rates than ordinary term loans.
Flexi loans account for about 2-2.5% of Tata Capital's book. Sabharwal said roughly 90% of this business serves micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs). Tata Capital has not reduced its revolving-credit exposure while awaiting the final rules.
Other NBFCs, including Aditya Birla Capital , Cholamandalam Investment and Finance Company and Shriram Finance , have indicated limited exposure to revolving credit products.
Aditya Birla Capital's NBFC chief Rakesh Singh said its exposure was very small and primarily concentrated in supply-chain financing and loans against shares. Cholamandalam's chief financial officer D Arul Selvan said revolving credit facilities accounted for just 0.6-0.7% of its loan book, or about ₹1,600 crore, largely comprising flexi-personal loans. Shriram Finance executive vice chairman Umesh Revankar also indicated that its exposure was limited, primarily comprising dealer trade advances. He estimated outstanding revolving credit facilities across NBFCs at about ₹2 lakh crore, against a total loan book of roughly ₹30 lakh crore.

docs.title: Himadri Speciality Chemical’s H1FY27 profit jumps 29%
docs.text:
Himadri Speciality Chemical is pairing sharp revenue growth with an ambitious industrial pivot, even as rising costs and heavier working capital needs weigh on cash generation. According to scanx.trade , the company’s latest half-year update shows a business that is still benefiting from strong demand in carbon materials, while simultaneously pushing hard into battery materials , carbon nanotubes and other higher-value products. 
 Half-year profit rises faster than costs, but cash remains tight 
For the first half of FY27, consolidated net profit increased 29 per cent year on year to ₹460 crore, supported by a 43 per cent rise in revenue to ₹3,123 crore. EBITDA moved up 30 per cent to ₹616 crore over the same period, suggesting that the topline expansion remained broad-based even as operating pressure became more visible in the quarter. 
 The second quarter alone was even more striking on the revenue line. Consolidated revenue climbed 57.93 per cent year on year to ₹1,691 crore, while EBITDA rose 27.48 per cent to ₹303 crore and profit after tax increased 31.33 per cent to ₹231 crore. On a standalone basis, Q2 revenue stood at ₹1,543 crore, EBITDA at ₹308 crore and profit after tax at ₹240 crore. 
 Yet the numbers also point to a clear trade-off. While sales momentum strengthened, operating efficiency softened sequentially. Management said EBITDA per metric tonne improved to ₹21,000 in the quarter from ₹17,900 a year earlier, but it was lower than the previous quarter’s level, reflecting pressure from freight costs, raw material movements and timing lags in price pass-through. 
 Carbon materials stayed the core engine 
The carbon materials and chemicals business continued to do the heavy lifting, contributing ₹1,539.02 crore to consolidated revenue in the quarter, up from ₹1,067.21 crore in the year-ago period. The power segment also expanded, with revenue rising to ₹33.32 crore from ₹22.90 crore. The “Others” category, which includes mining and related activities, brought in ₹144.14 crore in Q2FY27. 
 Capacity utilisation in the carbon black business was 88 per cent during the quarter. Management indicated a working range of 88 per cent to 95 per cent for the coming period, signalling that the business is still operating with some headroom even as demand stays firm. The company said volume growth accounted for 11 per cent of the topline increase, with the rest supported by higher value realisation and a richer product mix. 
 Battery materials and speciality products move to the forefront 
The bigger story, however, is the strategic shift under way outside traditional carbon black. Himadri is building an integrated platform in advanced materials, with a particular focus on battery-related chemistry and speciality applications. The company has commissioned a 200 MTPA anode material facility at Mahistikry in West Bengal, backed by more than a decade of in-house research and development. The plant has been designed with feedstock flexibility, allowing it to use internally developed materials, and early customer feedback on sample batches has reportedly been positive. 
 Work is also progressing on lithium iron phosphate cathode active materials. A 2,000 MTPA demonstration line is expected to be commissioned in Q3FY27, with a long-term target of 200,000 MTPA. The company has described this as one of the first commercial LFP CAM facilities outside China. In addition, a 40,000 TPA capacity is planned for commissioning next year to support scale-up after customer qualification. 
Another key project is India’s first commercial carbon nanotube plant, with 200 MTPA capacity and a planned commissioning in Q4FY27. The project carries a capex of ₹70 crore. Separately, the company is converting existing carbon black capacity to make super speciality carbon black, adding 6,000 MTPA of high-value output through a ₹170 crore investment, with commissioning targeted for Q4FY28. 
 Investments, overseas push and tyre business add new layers 
Beyond its own plants, the company has been deepening exposure to the battery value chain through investments and partnerships. It owns a 19.44 per cent stake in International Battery Company , which is moving from pre-revenue status towards revenue generation. The India Gigafactory project is expected to be operational in Q1FY28, and the venture is positioned as a technology partner for cell manufacturing rather than a captive consumption play alone. 
The company also has exposure to Sicona Battery Technologies , which recently secured AUD 45 million from the Australian Renewable Energy Agency . Sicona has completed the full acquisition of Advano in the United States, strengthening its silicon anode intellectual property and adding pilot plant capabilities in that market. Another investment, Invati Creations , where the stake stands at 40 per cent, is focused on high-performance electrode materials using nanotech-enabled formulations. 
To widen its international reach, a wholly owned subsidiary, Ardent Impex FZCO , has been incorporated in Dubai Airport Free Zone Area. The entity will handle global sales, marketing and procurement across the Middle East, Africa and Europe. On the downstream side, Birla Tyres , acquired in October 2023, is said to be nearing double-digit market share in select geographies. The brand now operates through 49 distributors, including 40 in India and nine overseas, and more than 1,300 dealers. Management expects entry into the passenger car radial segment by FY28. 
 Balance-sheet strain is visible despite stronger operating scale 
The half-year performance is not without strain. Trade receivables rose to ₹1,026.18 crore as of September 30, 2026, from ₹696.42 crore at the end of March 2026, while current borrowings increased to ₹1,152.26 crore. The company reported negative operating cash flow of ₹91.60 crore for H1FY27, largely because working capital absorbed ₹686.25 crore during the period.

docs.title: Manipur govt may declare armed groups involved in civilian violence unlawful: CM Yumnam Khemchand Singh
docs.text:
Guwahati: Manipur Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh chaired a security Review Meeting and stated the State Cabinet would be constrained to consider declaring such groups as unlawful if their involvement in violence against innocent civilians is established.
 The chief minister revised the prevailing law and order situation in the State and deliberated on measures to further strengthen security arrangements.
During the meeting, the Chief Minister directed security officers to identify the active armed groups , excluding those engaged in peace talks, suspected to be involved in the recent violence in the State. He instructed the security agencies to submit a detailed report on the involvement of these groups at the earliest. 
The Chief Minister further stated that, based on the findings of the report, the State Cabinet would be constrained to consider declaring such groups as unlawful if their involvement in violence against innocent civilians is established.
He also made it clear that necessary action would be initiated against any groups continuing to perpetrate violence against the civilian population. Such groups would be dealt with under the provisions of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), he added.
 Live Events
The meeting was attended by Home Minister Govindas Konthoujam; Chief Secretary Rajeev Singh Thakur; Security Advisor Kuldiep Singh; DGP, Manipur, Mukesh Singh; GOC, 3 Corps, Lt. General Girish Kalia, through Video Conferencing; ADGP (L&O); IGAR (S); IGAR (E); IG, CRPF, DIG BSF, SSB, ITBP; Joint Director IB, senior officers of central security agencies and officials of the Home Department.

Nifty ended Friday with sharp cuts amid selling pressure across the board, with consumer, IT and energy stocks dragging the markets the most. India VIX also moved back above its 200-DMA, indicating rising fear among the market participants. 
 Commenting on the technical charts, Rupak De, Senior Technical Analyst at LKP Securities, said that the setup has turned relatively cautious, with the index slipping below its 20-DMA for the first time in the past few sessions. Additionally, it has breached the 38.2% Fibonacci retracement of the prior up move from 24,571 to 26,341, he added. "With the index closing below the key support level of 25,500, the near-term bias appears weak, and there is potential for a decline toward the 25,000 mark in the short term. On the upside, immediate resistance is seen around 25,800," De said.
Here are 2 stock recommendations for Friday:
 Buy Kirloskar Oil Engines at Rs 1,375-1,385 | Upside: 5% | Target: Rs 1,500 | Stop Loss: Rs 1,320
 Kirloskar Oil Engines is currently taking a breakout of the rounding bottom formation on the daily time frame. The RSI is trending upward, reflecting positive momentum, and the stock finds support at the 21-day EMA, with all key EMAs rising. The stock is trading above important moving averages, indicating a bullish trend. 1,320 could work as an immediate support, and a hurdle can be seen at 1,500.

As preparations for the Union Budget 2026–27 gather pace, the groundwork underway signals a clear policy intent to accelerate domestic demand, revive private investment and generate employment, according to a budget note by Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL). The brokerage has identified five stocks across auto, agriculture, defence, financials and infrastructure themes, which it believes could deliver strong gains for investors.
 "The Budget is expected to focus on income-tax, GST, and customs simplification to enhance ease of doing business and support fiscal consolidation, alongside targeted support for agriculture, MSMEs, manufacturing, infrastructure, higher defence capex, EVs, and renewables through credit and incentives," the note authored by Research Analysts Sneha Poddar and Rekha Jaat said.
A strong capital expenditure thrust across highways, logistics, defence, rail freight corridors and connectivity is anticipated, complemented by emphasis on skilling, rural prosperity, women empowerment, AI adoption, climate action and digital finance to anchor India’s next phase of economic expansion, the note added.
The finance ministry started work on the Union Budget for 2026-27 from October 9 as per a circular issued by the Department of Economic Affairs (DEA).
The preparations come against the backdrop of an additional 50% US tariff on most Indian goods and other external headwinds. These have raised risks to India's growth and jobs outlook, prompting calls for stronger support to the export sector.
 Live Events
 5 stocks to buy: 
The stocks recommended by MOFSL are TVS Motor Company, UPL , Bharat Dynamics (BDL), M&M Financial Services and Dalmia Bharat , and each of these stocks has been assigned a 20% weight.
 1) TVS Motors: TVS Motors continues to outperform peers and is well-positioned to benefit from the budget’s push to boost domestic consumption and rural demand through higher allocations, income support, and infrastructure spending.
MOFSL said that improving rural sentiment, strong entry-level recovery and sustained two-wheeler demand will be key triggers. Moreover, the company's market share gains, easing discounts, and margin expansion will provide strong earnings visibility. The Apache and Ntorq maker remains its top pick in OEMs.
 2) UPL: The diversified agrochemical leader is well positioned to benefit from the union budget push riding on rural prosperity via higher agri credit, MSME support, and value-chain strengthening, lifting farmer incomes and crop-protection demand.
The company's strong points are stronger volumes, export tailwinds, improved working-capital discipline and post-bond-repayment balance-sheet strength, the brokerage note said. The company's rising focus on speciality chemicals supports solid 2HFY26 growth.
 3) Bharat Dynamics: Bharat Dynamics (BDL), a defence play, has a robust Rs 50,000 crore order pipeline over five years, with Rs 20,000 crore targeted in 2-3 years. This aligns with the expected defence capex surge and infra push.
The recent Rs 2.5 lakh crore DAC approvals for missiles, undersea warfare, and naval arms leverage BDL's tactical/strategic expertise, propelling FY31 turnover to Rs 100bn via indigenisation and lower provisions, the note said.
 4) M&M Financial Services: M&M Financial is poised for Union Budget 2026-27 benefits via rural prosperity, MSME credit, and employment focus, driving PV/tractor loan growth amid surging volumes from festive demand, GST cuts, and restocking.
The company targets Rs 3 lakh crore in assets under management (AUM) by 2030, which is at an 18-20% CAGR, bolstered by AI underwriting, lower credit costs, controlled opex, and margin stability for strong earnings visibility in retail portfolios.
 5) Dalmia Bharat: The cement company benefits from the budget’s infra capex surge, PMAY rural housing, and urban projects, driving cement volume growth.
Dalmia Bharat is a low-cost cement producer with high blending ratios, green power and low freight. The company is targeting 62 mtpa capacity by FY28, and its cost optimisation endeavours will likely lift EBITDA margins amid sector consolidation.

Reliance Power 's board of directors on Monday approved the issuance of up to 46.20 crore equity shares/warrants worth Rs 1,525 crore via preferential allotment mode.
 The board has set the issue price at Rs 33 per share.
The issue price of equity shares/warrants is at a discount of 13% over Monday's closing price of Rs 38.15 on the NSE. The announcement was made after market hours and Reliance Power shares on Monday ended with gains of Rs 1.81 or 4.98% over the previous closing price.
 Reliance Infrastructure Limited, the promoter of the company, will enhance its equity stake by over Rs 600 crore, a company filing said. The other investors in the preferential issue are Authum Investment and Infrastructure Limited and Sanatan Financial Advisory Services Private Limited.
The proceeds from the preferential issue will be utilised to expand business operations directly and/or through investment in subsidiaries and joint ventures, debt reduction and for general corporate purposes, the filing said.

The markets worldwide are waiting with bated breath on what will be a historic policy announcement from the US Federal Reserve , where the central bank is expected to usher in a rate cut cycle.
 The announcement will be made at 11:30 pm IST (Indian Standard Time) on Wednesday.
If analysts are to be believed, the US Fed is all but certain to cut interest rates for the first time in more than four years.
However, there is no consensus on the quantum of reduction. Some are predicting a smaller cut of a quarter of a percentage point, while others believe a bigger half-point reduction is in the works.
Senior officials at the US central bank, including Powell, have indicated that a rate cut is coming, as inflation eases toward the bank's long-term target of 2%, and the labour market continues to cool in the post-Covid economy.
 Live Events
If the Fed starts the rate cut cycle, the Reserve Bank of India is also expected to follow suit.
A smaller cut would be a more predictable move, while a bigger cut would do more to boost demand — while also running the risk of reigniting inflation.
 WATCH LIVE TODAY: Press conference with #FOMC Chair Powell at 2:30 p.m. ET: https://t.co/1uJrua5qsH https://t.co/FJa6TbkDMt pic.twitter.com/87g5NJITsz 
— Federal Reserve (@federalreserve) September 18, 2024 
By the end 2024, markets are expecting a total reduction of at least 100 basis points in the first rate cut cycle in over 4 years since 2020.
But whether the Fed goes for 25 or 50 bps, the biggest trigger for stock prices to move up or down would be Powell's motivation behind the cut.
Asset classes from stocks, currencies and fixed income could all log swings in the immediate aftermath of the Fed decision.
While easing US interest rates are directionally positive for equities in general, “we should keep in mind interest rates are just one variable in a complex adaptive system that determines the direction of Indian equity markets”, said Anoop Vijaykumar, Investments and Head of Research at Capitalmind.

 Stock recommendations for 4 November from MarketSmith India
 MarketSmith India 6 min read 4 Nov 2026, 06:00 AM IST 
 Summary
 MarketSmith India reveals its top stock recommendations for today, 4 November. Get expert insights into the best-performing stocks to guide your investment decisions. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 Stock market recap: Indian equities extended their rally for a fourth straight session on Tuesday, as a steep fall in crude oil prices, sustained foreign buying, and growing hopes of capital gains tax relief kept bulls firmly in control. 
 Nifty 50 rose 370.05 points, or 1.58%, to close at its day's high of 23,810.85, while Sensex jumped 1,225.07 points, or 1.62%, to settle at 76,917.85. Brent crude slipped to around $105 a barrel, about 11% below Friday's six-month high of $118, on optimism over diplomatic efforts to end the Iran conflict. 
 Foreign investors bought about ₹ 3,115 crore of Indian shares on Monday, adding to the momentum. Financials, FMCG , and Realty led the gains, while capital market stocks such as BSE jumped up to 8% on hopes of tax relief. Bharti Airtel rose about 5%, Asian Paints nearly 4%, and HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, and IndiGo about 3% each. IT, Metal, and Pharma stocks lagged, with ONGC, Power Grid, NTPC, and Sun Pharma among the losers, while Reliance saw mild profit-taking. Breadth was positive, with 2,127 stocks advancing, 1,477 stocks declining, and 109 remaining unchanged. The U.S. midterm election results, due after Indian market hours, will be closely watched.
 Two stock recommendations by MarketSmith India: 
 Buy: Garware Hi-Tech Films Limited (current price: ₹ 7,395) 
 Why it’s recommended: Strong growth in high-margin specialty films (Paint Protection Films, Sun Control Films and Architectural Films) supported by capacity expansion and backward integration into TPU manufacturing. The global export-led business has a presence in 90+ countries and vertically integrated manufacturing, providing pricing power, cost efficiencies, and market-share gains in specialty films. 
 Key metrics : P/E: 37.97, 52-week high: ₹ 7,990.00, volume: ₹ 73.51 crore 
 Technical analysis: Trendline Breakout 
 Risk factors: Exposure to volatility in crude-linked raw material prices and foreign exchange fluctuations due to significant export dependence. Regulatory risks in the sun-control film segment and demand sensitivity to automotive and construction industry cycles. 
 Buy: ₹ 7,321–7,432 
 Target price : ₹ 9,300 in two to three months 
 Stop loss : ₹ 6,800 
 Buy: CORONA Remedies Limited (current price: ₹ 2,271) 
 Why it’s recommended : Strong positioning in chronic and sub-chronic therapies (women's healthcare, cardio-diabetes, pain management and urology), which contribute over 70% of revenue and continue to outperform the Indian Pharma Market. A robust brand portfolio with leading “engine brands,” new product launches, and expansion into biologics/biosimilars supporting sustained market-share gains and revenue growth. 
 Key metrics: P/E: 60.38, 52-week high: ₹ 2,294.00, volume: ₹ 23.72 crore 
 Technical analysis: Cup base pattern breakout 
 Risk factors: Heavy dependence on the domestic Indian market and key therapeutic segments, making growth vulnerable to pricing pressure and competitive intensity. Reliance on third-party contract manufacturers/suppliers and ongoing pharmaceutical regulatory compliance risks. 
 Buy at: ₹ 2,248–2,282 
 Target price : ₹ 2,900 in two to three months 
 Stop loss: ₹ 2,088 
 How Nifty 50 Performed 
 On Tuesday, Indian equity markets rallied, with Nifty 50 surging 370.05 points (1.58%) to close at 23,810.85, reflecting robust buying interest across several sectors. The benchmark opened at 23,582.25, touched an intraday low of 23,482.80, and climbed to the day's high of 23,810.85, indicating sustained upward momentum and a strong finish. Sectoral performance was largely positive, led by FMCG (+3.65%), Realty (+2.33%), Private Banks (+1.98%), Financial Services (+1.89%), and Auto (+1.71%). Meanwhile, PSU Banks (-1.27%) and Metals (-0.14%) underperformed. Broader market sentiment remained constructive, with 2,127 stocks advancing, 1,477 stocks declining, and 109 remaining unchanged. This translates into an advance-decline ratio of approximately 1.44:1, highlighting healthy market participation. 
 Nifty 50 witnessed a strong bullish session, forming a sizable bullish candle on the daily chart and closing at the day's high, indicating aggressive buying interest. The index has staged a sharp recovery from its recent October lows, with improving price action suggesting a potential short-term trend reversal. Notably, the index reclaimed its key short- and medium-term moving averages and is testing a significant descending trendline, while remaining below its long-term 200-DMA. A sustained move above the descending trendline would strengthen the case for a broader bullish reversal. The Relative Strength Index (RSI) rose sharply to 66.59, reflecting strengthening buying momentum without entering overbought territory. Meanwhile, the MACD has registered a bullish crossover, with an expanding positive histogram, indicating accelerating upward momentum and improving trend strength. 
 Nifty 50 staged a strong rebound from lower levels, closing above its 100-day moving average (100-DMA), signalling renewed buying interest and improving near-term market sentiment. Technically, the recovery indicates strengthening bullish momentum, although sustained follow-through buying will be crucial to confirm a further upward move. On the upside, 24,000–24,400 is expected to act as key resistance, where selling pressure could emerge. Conversely, 23,500–23,400 is likely to provide immediate support, making it an important zone to monitor for the sustainability of the ongoing recovery.

 Stock market recap: The benchmark Sensex rallied 1,233 points to a more than seven-week high on Monday, extending its gains for a third consecutive session. The Nifty 50 also climbed above 23,400, buoyed by a sharp rally in Reliance Industries following its quarterly earnings and easing crude oil prices.
 The 30-share Sensex surged 1,233.25 points, or 1.66%, to close at the day's high of 75,692.78, its highest level since 7 September. The Nifty rose 387.70 points, or 1.68%, to settle at 23,440.80, also its highest close in more than five weeks.
 Among the 30 Sensex constituents, Reliance Industries led the gains, surging 11.64% after reporting a record quarterly profit of ₹ 29,550 crore for July-September, up 33.8% from a year earlier. Strong performance in its oil-to-chemicals business, driven by higher global fuel margins, and growth in its telecom arm offset relatively subdued performance in retail.
 Two stock recommendations by MarketSmith India: 
 Buy: Tanla Platforms Ltd (current price: ₹ 644) 
 Why it’s recommended: Strong leadership in India’s CPaaS and enterprise messaging market, rising digital communication, RCS and OTT messaging adoption, and the scaling of proprietary platforms such as Wisely and AI-driven communication solutions could improve margins and create new revenue streams. 
 Key metrics: P/E: 15.01, 52-week high: ₹ 656.00, volume: ₹ 87.28 crore 
 Technical analysis: Cup base formation and trendline breakout 
 Risk factors: Regulatory changes by TRAI or telecom operators may impact messaging volumes, pricing and profitability, while high dependence on telecom partners and intense competition from global CPaaS players could pressure growth and margins. 
 Buy: ₹ 638-647 
 Target price: ₹ 750 in two to three months 
 Stop loss: ₹ 595 
 Buy: Leela Palaces Hotels & Resorts Ltd (current price: ₹ 671) 
 Why it’s recommended: Rising demand for luxury hospitality in India, limited premium hotel supply, strong luxury brand positioning, and expansion through new hotels and management contracts support higher occupancy, room rates and long-term growth visibility. 
 Key metrics: P/E: 45.18, 52-week high: ₹ 683.00, volume: ₹ 156.45 crore 
 Technical analysis: Trendline Breakout 
 Risk factors: Luxury hotel demand is cyclical and vulnerable to economic slowdowns, travel disruptions and geopolitical events, while execution risks in expansion projects and increasing competition from domestic and international luxury hotel chains may affect returns. 
 Buy at: ₹ 664-674 
 Target price: ₹ 850 in two to three months 
 Stop loss: ₹ 625 
 How Nifty 50 performed 
 Indian equity markets ended Monday's session on a strong note, with the Nifty 50 surging 387.70 points, or 1.68%, to close at 23,440.80, against its previous close of 23,053.10. The index opened at 23,222.30, touched an intraday low of 23,207.05 and closed at the day's high, indicating strong buying momentum towards the end of the session.
 Broader market participation was encouraging, with 2,445 stocks advancing, 1,164 declining and 104 remaining unchanged, translating into an advance-decline ratio of 2.10:1. Sectoral indices were largely in the green, led by Nifty Oil & Gas (+5.95%), Metal (+3.21%), Consumer Durables (+2.70%), PSU Bank (+1.36%) and Auto (+1.33%). Media (-0.76%), IT (-0.50%) and Private Bank (-0.14%) were among the few sectors that ended lower.
 The Nifty 50 formed a strong bullish candle on the daily chart, closing at the session's high. Its sharp recovery from recent lows points to renewed buying interest and improving short-term momentum. The index has reclaimed its 20-day and 50-day exponential moving averages (EMAs), signalling a possible near-term trend reversal. However, it continues to trade below its 100-day and 200-day moving averages, suggesting that the broader trend remains cautious.
 The index's prevailing downward price structure has shown initial signs of improvement, although a sustained breakout above the broader declining trendline is yet to be confirmed. The relative strength index (RSI) has strengthened to 61.03, moving above the neutral 50 mark and its signal average. This indicates improving bullish momentum without the index entering overbought territory. Meanwhile, the moving average convergence divergence (MACD) has registered a bullish crossover, with an expanding positive histogram pointing to strengthening upward momentum, although the MACD line remains below the zero line.
 The Nifty's recovery above its 50-day moving average (50-DMA) signals renewed buying interest and improving near-term sentiment. However, sustained buying will be crucial to confirm further gains.
 On the upside, the 23,600-23,700 range is likely to act as a key resistance zone, where selling pressure could emerge. On the downside, the 23,200-23,000 range is expected to provide immediate support and will be important in determining whether the ongoing recovery can be sustained.
 How did the Nifty Bank perform? 
 Bank Nifty began the week on a firm note, opening higher at 54,837.20 before absorbing early selling pressure to hit an intraday low of 54,582.00. The index subsequently recovered steadily to touch a high of 55,046.35 and closed at 55,002.20, up 315.25 points, or 0.58%, near the day's high. The recovery suggests that buyers are stepping in at lower levels. The index also closed just above its 21-day moving average (DMA).
 State-owned lenders led the gains, with Bank of Baroda (+2.75%), State Bank of India (+2.61%) and HDFC Bank (+1.04%) among the major gainers. Howeve

docs.text:
NSE shares opened at ₹ 1,786 per share today, as compared to previous close of ₹ 1,779 on Monday and touched an intraday high of ₹ 1,794 on 3 November. The stock has jumped over 3% in a month and over 4% in two weeks.
The newly listed stock also witnessed a spurt in its trading volume. According to data available on NSE, around 7.81 lakh shares changed hands during the intraday session on Tuesday.
The stock rally also came in amid positive sentiments on Dalal Street. Indian equity markets opened higher for the second consecutive session on Tuesday, extending their upward momentum as investors drew confidence from improving second-quarter earnings, a return of foreign institutional investors (FIIs) to buying, and a moderation in crude oil prices. The Nifty 50 opened at 23,582.25, advancing 141.45 points or 0.60%, while the BSE Sensex began the session at 76,288.65, gaining 595.87 points or 0.79%.
NSE share price listed on the stock market with an opening listing price of ₹ 1,840 per share (delivering a 0.84% premium over its IPO price range of ₹ 1,700 to ₹ 1,785).
Brokerage firm Kantilal Chhaganlal Securities has given a ‘buy’ rating to the NSE stock with a target price of ₹ 2205, seeing an upside potential up to 25% in the long-term.
“NSE’s capital-light, technology-led model provides strong operating leverage, supporting high margins, cash generation and return ratios as volumes and ancillary businesses scale. While index-options market-share erosion and regulatory changes remain key monitorable, NSE’s entrenched leadership and diversified ecosystem provide resilience against volatility in any single segment also NSE adopted Cost saving method . We estimate ~13.5% revenue CAGR over FY26–29E and value NSE at 35x FY29E P/E, arriving at a Target Price of ₹ 2,205,” the firm said in a note.
The bidding period for the NSE IPO commenced on September 17, 2026, and concluded on September 21, 2026.
NSE IPO received a subscription of 5.71 times on the final day of bidding, according to exchange data available. Investors placed bids for 505.81 million shares against the 88.6 million shares offered, with institutional and high-net-worth investors contributing significantly to the demand.
The NSE IPO had a price band of ₹ 1,700 to ₹ 1,785 per equity share, with a face value of Re 1 per share. The lot size was set at 8 equity shares, and investors were allowed to bid in multiples of 8 shares thereafter.
The IPO consisted entirely of an offer for sale (OFS) of existing shares, with no fresh equity issuance. Consequently, the proceeds from the offering, after accounting for issue-related expenses, were to be received by the selling shareholders. The primary objective of the IPO was to facilitate the OFS and enable the listing of NSE's equity shares on the BSE.
Kotak Mahindra Capital Co. Ltd. acted as the book-running lead manager for the issue, while MUFG Intime India Pvt. Ltd. served as the registrar.

docs.title: Muhurat Trading Picks: Adani Ports, Info Edge to Kotak Bank - ICICI Sec recommends these 10 stocks to buy on Diwali
docs.text:
It expects the Nifty 50 to deliver healthy double-digit returns over the next 12 months, with quality mid- and small-cap stocks offering opportunities as markets increasingly shift their focus from liquidity and valuations to earnings delivery.
The brokerage's Muhurat Trading picks include Venus Pipes and Tubes, Kotak Mahindra Bank, Zydus Lifesciences, Info Edge, Adani Ports and SEZ, Apollo Micro Systems, Neogen Chemicals, Indian Hotels, Saregama India and Ethos.
ICICI Securities expects Kotak Mahindra Bank to deliver 20–22% advances growth, supported by a gradual recovery in net interest margins and sustained moderation in credit costs. These factors are likely to drive earnings growth and improve return on assets (RoA) over FY27–FY28, the brokerage said.
The brokerage values the standalone bank at 2.4 times its FY28 book value and its subsidiaries at ₹ 127 per share. It has maintained a Buy rating on the stock with a target price of ₹ 540.
Key risks: ICICI Securities flagged two key risks: an adverse change in the business mix that could dilute margins, and slower-than-expected business growth.
ICICI Securities noted that Venus Pipes and Tubes has recently completed a fresh equity raise through a preferential allotment, with the proceeds primarily intended to pare debt. This is expected to significantly strengthen the company's balance sheet and could make it net debt-free in FY27E. The resulting reduction in interest expenses is likely to support profitability and prove accretive to earnings per share (EPS), the brokerage said.
The brokerage expects Venus Pipes to sustain strong growth across its established businesses as well as emerging segments, driven by strategic diversification and an expanding portfolio of niche products. It also highlighted the company's improving balance sheet, expected to turn net cash-positive, and its healthy double-digit return ratios as key positives.
On the back of these growth prospects, ICICI Securities has reiterated its BUY recommendation on the stock with a target price of ₹ 2,340, based on a valuation of 30 times its estimated FY28 earnings.
Key risks: A slowdown in the capital expenditure cycle across end-user industries and global geopolitical tensions that could trigger intermittent business volatility.
ICICI Securities expects the company's upcoming product launches to offset the waning momentum of its earlier launches and support the next phase of growth. The brokerage highlighted the rare and orphan disease segment as a key emerging opportunity, which could strengthen the company's growth prospects over the coming years.
With its key business segments expected to remain resilient and a pipeline of new launches providing additional growth drivers, ICICI Securities believes the company is well-positioned for sustained growth. It has assigned a BUY rating with a target price of ₹ 1,480, valuing the stock at 28 times its estimated FY28 earnings per share (EPS) of ₹ 52.9.
Key risks: The brokerage flagged potential delays in the launch of niche products, particularly in the US market, and the possibility that higher research and development spending on innovative products may generate lower-than-expected returns.
ICICI Securities believes Neogen Chemicals has the capabilities across both electrolytes and salts to cater to the requirements of Indian battery manufacturers seeking to indigenise battery material production. With the necessary ecosystem in place to tap opportunities in the electric vehicle (EV) space, the brokerage sees Neogen as an attractive investment proposition.
The brokerage has assigned a BUY rating on the stock with a target price of ₹ 2,765, valuing the company at 20 times its estimated FY28 EBITDA.
Key risks: ICICI Securities highlighted delays in the ramp-up or offtake of the battery chemicals business and volatility in the prices of key raw materials, particularly bromine and lithium, as potential risks.
ICICI Securities expects Info Edge to deliver a revenue CAGR of around 14.8% over FY26–FY28, with margins projected to improve to 44% by FY28 from 40.9% in FY26. The brokerage believes the company is well-positioned to benefit from a sustained recovery in recruitment demand, better monetisation of AI-led offerings and a gradual improvement in profitability at 99acres and its matchmaking business.
It also sees potential value unlocking from the company's investment portfolio, which could provide an additional upside trigger. Based on these growth prospects, ICICI Securities has assigned a BUY rating to the stock, with a target price of ₹ 1,530, derived from a sum-of-the-parts (SoTP) valuation.
Key risks: The brokerage flagged a slower-than-expected recovery in recruitment and hiring activity, along with continued weakness in Shiksha due to AI-driven disruption in search traffic.
ICICI Securities expects Saregama India's EBITDA margin to improve gradually, driven by operating leverage, to 34.7% in FY27 and 35.5% in FY28, compared with 34.2% in FY26. The brokerage expects healthy revenue growth, coupled with stable margins, to translate into an earnings CAGR of around 25% over FY26–FY28, alongside an improvement in return ratios.
The brokerage has assigned a BUY rating on the stock with a target price of ₹ 650, valuing it at 38 times its estimated FY28 earnings per share (EPS).  India seeks clearer evidence of air pollution's health impact as smog worsens
 Priyanka Sharma , Vijay C Roy 4 min read 3 Nov 2026, 04:13 PM IST 
 Summary
 The health ministry has directed states to strengthen screening and tracking of pollution-linked illnesses through standardised disease coding, regular reporting and follow-up of high-risk patients.

 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.

 NEW DELHI: As toxic smog pushes air pollution back into the public-health spotlight across northern India, the health ministry has directed states and Union territories to step up tracking of pollution-linked illnesses, requiring hospitals to screen patients, use standardised disease codes and report cases regularly.
 The move seeks to build a clearer picture of air pollution's effects on respiratory and cardiovascular health amid worsening air quality and growing concerns over its long-term health costs.
 Under the new guidelines, hospitals running cardio-respiratory health effects screening and treatment (Chest) clinics will have to maintain daily patient records, classify cases using World Health Organization ( WHO ) codes, and submit regular reports to health authorities, according to two officials and a ministry communication seen by Mint .
 Hospitals will submit daily patient numbers to district and state health authorities, which will share the data monthly with the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC). The ministry has also mandated fortnightly progress reviews with states and linked Chest clinics with Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (AAMs) to facilitate follow-up of high-risk patients through ASHA workers, the officials said.
 Clinicians will use the WHO's International Classification of Diseases (ICD) codes to record asymptomatic exposure, symptomatic cases and pollution-associated illnesses. The standardized system is intended to create a more consistent record of pollution-related health effects.
 The Centre runs the National Programme on Climate Change and Human Health (NPCCHH) through the NCDC. The programme provides “a structured approach for screening, diagnosis, management and counselling for air pollution related illnesses in patients of all age groups through establishment of chest clinics at District Hospital and Medical College Hospitals from September to February of each year,” the ministry said in its communication to states and Union territories.
 The guidelines call for “screening and risk communication for air pollution-related illnesses” and establishing “possible causes (including air pollution) and confirm diagnosis”, alongside ensuring the “indenting and stocking of essential equipment, drugs and consumables”.
 Queries sent to the health ministry spokesperson and the NCDC remained unanswered till press time.
 The scale of health burden 
 The surveillance push comes amid mounting evidence of the health toll from air pollution. A 2024 study published in The Lancet Planetary Health estimated that long-term exposure to fine particulate matter caused roughly 16.6 million deaths in India between 2009 and 2019, averaging 1.5 million annually under WHO safety guidelines.
 Exposure to these pollutants is associated with stroke, cardiovascular and respiratory diseases, lung cancer and a higher risk of premature death, according to experts.
 The urgency is particularly visible in Delhi-NCR, where the air quality index (AQI) reached 332, in the 'very poor' category, at 9.05am on 3 November, according to the Central Pollution Control Board's SAMEER app. Jahangirpuri recorded a 'severe' reading of 452.
 The deterioration from 117 on 31 October to 324 on 2 November prompted the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) to invoke Stage II of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP), deploying mechanical sweeping, water sprinkling with dust suppressants and hotspot inspections.
 Environmentalists, however, say administrative enforcement must accompany health surveillance.
 “Appropriate action must be taken in accordance with the law, including penal action wherever necessary, against polluting industries operating in non-conforming areas and on agricultural land in Delhi,” said Paras Tyagi, co-founder of the Centre for Youth Culture Law and Environment. Resident welfare associations (RWAs) and civil society groups must also be involved in reporting violations, he added.
 The challenge 
 Health experts caution that tracking pollution-related illnesses is only part of the response. Effective intervention requires coordinated action across regions, rather than isolated measures by individual cities or states.
 "There is no doubt about the devastating health impacts of air pollution, which contributes to nearly two million deaths annually in India. When levels spike, hospitals see immediate surges in asthma, COPD exacerbations, and heart attacks. While tracking clinic data is a good step, data collection alone is not enough—we need urgent, coordinated action,” said Dr. Sowmya Swaminathan, former WHO chief scientist and former ICMR director general.
 Swaminathan stressed that tackling pollution requires coordinated, multi-year action across the Indo-Gangetic airshed, covering transport, industry, dust, clean cooking fuel and stubble burning, rather than isolated efforts by Delhi and neighbouring states.
 There is also a clinical challenge in determining how much of a patient's illness can be attributed specifically to air pollution, doctors say. Respiratory symptoms can have multiple triggers, making it difficult to isolate the contribution of polluted air.
 "Over the past week, we have seen a sharp rise in patient footfalls suffering from acute respiratory allergies and severe asthma exacerbations," said Dr. Dhiren Gupta, senior consultant and co-director, paediatric ICU at Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, New Delhi.

Global 
 People are using AI for divorce advice and it’s driving their lawyers crazy
 Dalvin Brown , The Wall Street Journal 6 min read 3 Nov 2026, 06:45 AM IST 
 Summary
 Feed one side of a family fight into a chatbot and you might get the legal answer you want to see, but it won’t necessarily fly with the judge. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 Steven Benmor, a Toronto family lawyer, recently drafted a prenuptial agreement the way he said his client asked. Then the client emailed him a 13-part list of revisions nearly as long as the prenup.
 Some revisions went so deep into the weeds, Benmor said, that no human could have come up with them. Benmor knew his client had turned to an artificial intelligence chatbot. And he knew that taking the time to explain why the chatbot was mistaken would require charging his client extra.
 His mantra: “Don’t spend money unduly by asking a human expert to enter into a debate with a robot expert.”
 It was hardly the first time this had happened to Benmor. Family lawyers, who handle everything from prenups to divorces and custody fights, say many of their clients are now showing up with pages of legal advice that look like the result of ChatGPT or other chatbots.
 In a spring survey of 133 lawyers at Cordell & Cordell, a national family-law firm, 80% said clients had sent them correspondence, draft pleadings or strategy suggestions they believed were generated with AI.
 People ask chatbots for everything these days, including financial advice and medical diagnoses. But family law isn’t a place where they shine, lawyers say. Feed one side of a family fight into a chatbot and you might get the legal answer you want to see, even if it isn’t one that will necessarily fly with the judge.
 Divorcing partners turn to them anyway. Money is often tight for people when a marriage comes apart, and hiring a lawyer takes time. A chatbot answers right away, even in the middle of the night.
 Logan Burns used ChatGPT for legal advice and ended up having to apologize to the judge. Burns, a 35-year-old pastor and roofing salesman in LaGrange, Ga., paid a Georgia lawyer a $2,500 retainer when his marriage came apart last year. The couple called off the divorce and tried to reconcile, and his wife took the children to stay with family in Montana. When the reconciliation failed, the custody fight landed there, where a lawyer wanted $7,000. He paid $19.99 a month for the chatbot instead.
 “It was doing the job of a lawyer, or at least a paralegal,” he said.
 ChatGPT pointed him to a rule that generally lets a state decide custody once a child has lived there for six months. His children had been in Montana for less than that. Burns wanted the case moved to Georgia.
 So he wrote the judge a letter arguing that the court had improperly taken over his children’s case. The judge brought it up in court. “You technically don’t have jurisdiction,” Burns recalled telling the judge. The judge sternly told him that wasn’t how it worked. The rule has exceptions: Courts can step in during emergencies, and Burns had filed an emergency request himself.
 “Your Honor, I’m not accusing you of anything,” he recalled saying. “ChatGPT gave me the baseline information. But it doesn’t give you the interpretation of law.”
 He has temporary custody of his children, though the case is ongoing. “Thank you, AI,” Burns said.
 Damien Charlotin, an adjunct professor at UC Law San Francisco who tracks AI-generated errors in court cases, has counted 148 family-law rulings in which judges flagged fake citations or other apparent AI mistakes. More than 100 came this year.
 Chatbots also tend to take one side’s word at face value, even though two sides often disagree on facts in family law. The owner of an online wellness company had agreed in his divorce to pay hefty spousal support, based on what the business was earning. Years later, taking far less money out of the business, he asked a chatbot whether a judge would cut his payments. The bot told him he had an easy win.
 The chatbot never asked to see his financial statements, or his spending, which hadn’t shrunk with his income. It “simply accepted our client’s narrative regarding his finances,” said Hossein Berenji, a Los Angeles family lawyer whose firm later took the case.
 Relying on the chatbot’s advice, he hired a lawyer and persuaded the attorney to follow the chatbot’s strategy. In late 2024, the lawyer asked the court to reduce the support, attaching some company records. The other side’s lawyer used those same records to argue his income hadn’t really fallen, and about a year later the judge agreed. The man blamed his lawyer, not the chatbot, and switched to Berenji’s firm. “It took us a while to convince him to move away from what AI was advising him to do,” Berenji said.
 The firm brought in a forensic accountant, who found what the first filing had left out: A lot of the company’s products had spoiled while the business was still paying its overhead, Berenji said. Sales were big. What was left for his client wasn’t.
 At a recent hearing, a judge tentatively agreed his finances had changed and put his support payments on hold for now.
 What the chatbot called an easy win took two law firms and nearly two years.
 Everything the man paid his first lawyer was “basically money thrown down the drain,” and he likely overpaid spousal support the whole time, Berenji said.

 The filings appeared to be written by AI, Kamal said. “It was scaring my client.”

docs.text:
Mint Money 
 Silver fall: what drove the crash, what's next and what should investors do?
 Jash Kriplani 6 min read 3 Nov 2026, 01:25 PM IST 
 Summary
 Silver ETFs have corrected sharply as speculative positions unwind and bond yields rise. Here's what drove the fall, what could shape the outlook and how investors should approach the metal. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 If last year's silver rally tempted you to join in, this year's slide offers a sobering lesson. Silver ETFs have corrected more than 50% from their highs earlier this year, leaving investors who entered near the peak nursing steep losses.
 The reversal underscores why silver should remain a small part of a diversified portfolio. Driven by both industrial and investment demand, the metal can be highly volatile. Experts attribute the recent correction to the unwinding of speculative positions and rising US bond yields, which have dulled the appeal of non-yielding assets such as silver.
 What drove the fall?
 Silver prices are driven by two factors: industrial demand and investment demand. “Right now both drivers are seeing some pullback. Industrial demand is slowing due to easing demand from the renewable space and investment demand is easing as several silver ETFs globally have seen redemptions,” said a fund manager, requesting anonymity.
 Investor redemptions can partly be attributed to rising bond yields. Typically, when yields rise, commodities such as gold and silver lose their appeal because they do not offer any income.
 “As long as we are talking about higher interest rates and higher inflation, the fall could be capped,” said Manav Modi, analyst, precious metal research at Motilal Oswal Financial Services.
 With US inflation expected to remain elevated, markets expect the Federal Reserve to keep interest rates higher for longer, with further hikes possible. “High inflation, a hawkish Fed and high bond yields are drawing investors away from gold and silver towards US Treasuries. In this situation, silver prices could stay in the current range. The Fed's stance in December will decide the outlook from here,” said Tapan Patel, fund manager – commodities, Tata Mutual Fund.
 “In the near term, prices may remain volatile due to the Fed’s hawkish stance, expectations of higher interest rates for longer and concerns over global economic growth. Unlike gold, silver is also driven by industrial demand, making it more sensitive to economic conditions,” said Satish Dondapati, fund manager, Kotak MF.
 On the industrial side, silver remains in a supply deficit this year, a situation expected to continue next year. However, ETF redemptions have helped bridge the near-term gap.
 “When an ETF is redeemed, the fund house has to release the physical metal into the market. So while the long-term deficit story continues, near-term silver availability is fairly comfortable. Solar demand grew at a very strong pace in 2024 and 2025, and it has levelled off this year. The deficit has narrowed, but it is still a deficit market,” said the fund manager quoted above. He added that if global economic activity holds up in 2027, silver's demand-supply fundamentals could improve.
 Copper adds to the overhang. Bulk of silver is produced as a by-product of copper, zinc and gold mining. The International Copper Study Group, in October, forecast a surplus in the copper market for 2027.
 “Silver needs a push from either gold or copper. Either the interest rate and inflation picture must turn supportive for gold to rise and silver to follow, or copper supply must tighten,” said Modi.
 What lies ahead? 
 Despite the correction, silver ETFs are still up about 20% over a one-year period, and silver has outperformed gold in recent years. According to the fund manager quote above, about two-thirds of the silver produced is consumed by industrial demand, leaving a relatively limited free float for coins, bars and ETFs. 
 “When a large amount of money enters or leaves ETFs, it amplifies the price moves. As a rule of thumb, silver's volatility tends to be one-and-a-half to two times that of gold,” said the fund manager.
 The sharp run-up also attracted speculative money. The unwinding of these positions is now adding to selling pressure.
 The outlook will depend on how interest rates, inflation and industrial demand evolve. A more supportive rate environment could revive investment demand, while stronger global economic activity could improve industrial demand. Conversely, persistently high yields and weak industrial demand could keep prices under pressure.
 How should investors respond?
 For investors still building their precious metals allocation and looking to add silver, experts suggest staggered purchases rather than investing a lump sum. Given its volatility, silver should generally account for a smaller share of a portfolio than gold.
 “Silver is very high beta. Overall precious metals can be up to 10-15% of the portfolio, split roughly 70:30 between gold and silver. Investors may accumulate silver gradually for the long term, but it should be held for diversification, not as a return enhancer. Chasing returns can backfire,” said Patel.
 “Avoid lump-sum investments and consider staggered buying on corrections. Given its higher volatility compared to gold, conservative investors should keep a smaller allocation to silver within a diversified portfolio,” said Dondapati of Kotak MF.
 Near-term volatility may persist amid global uncertainty. Investors should therefore treat silver as a diversifier within a broader portfolio rather than chase its recent returns.

docs.title: Rising interest rates: should you borrow or delay festive season purchases?

Mint Money 
 Rising interest rates: should you borrow or delay festive season purchases?
 Raj Khosla 4 min read 3 Nov 2026, 10:19 AM IST 
 Summary
 Looking ahead, we can be almost certain of additional increases in repo rates and the consequent hikes in cost of loans. We should factor in the uncertainties while making decisions around our future financial commitments. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 Following the US Federal Reserve’s move to raise benchmark rates in September, the Reserve Bank of India announced an increase of 25 basis points in the policy repo rate on 7 October. Typically, such increases signal that interest rates are set to rise for a range of financial products, including loans and deposits. 
 Big-ticket corporate loans follow their own evaluation dynamics regardless of rising or falling rates. Consumer credit, however, reacts almost immediately to changes in interest rates and thus has a real-time impact on our day-to-day living standards. What should you buy? Property, vehicle, jewellery, electronic items, travel? And equally importantly, when should the purchase be made? 
 The timing of the recent increase coincides with enhanced consumer spending, which is the usual concomitant of any festive season. Online and offline retailers offer their best deals during this period to capitalise on higher customer spending. On top of that, lenders make life more exciting by providing quick and easy loans to drive spending during the auspicious season. Not to miss out on the festivities, credit cards also offer instant discounts on purchases with low- or zero-cost EMIs.
 The increase in interest rates will not only impact new borrowers, but existing loan EMIs will also increase for loans linked to the benchmark interest rates. Consequently, you may then find less money available to splurge during the festive season. Do consider delaying non-essential spending. 
 The purpose of your intended borrowing has a direct bearing on the decision whether taking on debt is a good idea. Several banks run special festive offers where they provide discounts on processing fees, lower interest rates and enhanced tenures. If you have decided to borrow, you should make the most of the seasonal offers, thereby lowering the overall cost of your loan. 
 Although it is different strokes for different folks, scenarios where a loan makes sense for most individuals: 
 While buying an asset, always ensure that loans add value to your life. Buying a home is usually a great idea, since it not only saves on immediate rental costs but also provides long-term appreciation and also serves up a sense of mental security. 
 Festive offers can provide an excellent opportunity for savings through debt consolidation. A process where multiple high-interest loans are combined into a single loan at a lower interest rate. For example, multiple credit card outstandings and high-interest personal loans can be grouped into a single loan at a lower interest rate via a gold loan, or a more efficiently priced personal loan. 
 Festive season or not, medical emergencies and accidents come unannounced. When there is an inadequate emergency fund, a swiftly disbursed personal loan can help in settling your immediate medical expenses. In recent times, personal loan disbursals have well & truly come of age, and can be remitted to your bank in a couple of hours.
 It is always a good idea to check and compare the available options to ensure you get the best deal available. Marketplace platforms do allow you to easily compare the overall costs involved, not just the headline interest rate. Customers should always evaluate the flexibility offered by the loan provider regarding penalty-free part-payments and premature loan closures. 
 Customers should rationally identify their individual requirements and thus avoid falling into a debt trap owing to a combination of enticing retail offers and easy credit available at favourable terms. During the festive season, it is almost incumbent upon most of us to somehow throw caution to the wind. An impulsive purchase of non-essential items should be avoided, as the total outlay can be higher than what was initially planned and may, therefore, place a burden beyond your repayment capacity. This is especially true in a rising interest rate environment. 
 The current 0.25% increase in benchmark lending rates may dampen the mood around certain credit-led purchases. However, a much larger impact on consumer demand will be caused by macroeconomic factors – a combination of inflation, contraction of disposable household incomes, diminishing consumer sentiment and reducing availability of cheap credit. 
 Looking ahead, we can be almost certain of additional increases in repo rates and the consequent hikes in cost of loans. Global headwinds will continue to create unrelenting inflationary pressure, and coupled with the artificial intelligence-led disruptions, we will face unexpected challenges. We should factor in these uncertainties while making decisions around our future financial commitments.
 Raj Khosla is managing director, MyMoneyMantra. Views are personal.
